result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Answer B covers every part of the guarantee: claim window, how to claim, a re-visit within a set time, a refund and when payment is due. It leaves every term the owner didn't give as a visible placeholder, so the owner can only publish promises they can keep. Answer A is persuasive and comes with useful publishing checks, but its copy states invented commitments as fact: a 7-day window, a full refund, pay-after with no deposit, photos of every job and blanket damage coverage. It never sets a response time for the return visit. B also says the work is done by the two owners who live in Eastbrook, which the brief doesn't confirm, but it invents no numbers. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Answer A states what the guarantee covers, how to claim and what Halyard does in return. It leaves every term the brief didn't give (claim window, return time, refund scope, payment timing) as a visible placeholder, and it adds a short booking-button version. Answer B is persuasive and its publishing checklist is useful. But its guarantee text commits the owner to a fixed 7-day window, no deposit, pay-after, before-and-after photos and damage coverage, none of which the owner gave. Only some of these are flagged afterward, so the owner could publish promises they can't keep.
